title: upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations + scheduling tweaks
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and token-cost for medium-to-long sequence workloads by adopting FlashAttentionV2 kernels, adding fused query/key/value projection->matmul fusions for common model patterns, and improving rotary/rope handling to avoid redundant rotations in the KV cache path. This PR also includes scheduler hints to improve continuous batching effectiveness for mixed-seq workloads.

Changes in this PR: consolidated into a single description string per PR requirements. Highlights: adopt FlashAttentionV2 kernels where hardware supports it, fall back to our optimized FlashAttentionV1 path for older kernels; implement fused QKV->matmul kernels with optional int8/float16 fast-paths; fuse rotary embedding application into the attention forward pass to avoid separate tensor ops during generation; add KV-cache-safe rotary caching so cached keys/values store pre-rotated tensors and avoid re-applying rotations on each decode step; scheduler hints: introduce per-model sequence distribution telemetry and a new continuous-batcher policy that prefers grouping compatible seq-len buckets to reduce padding; add runtime flags to opt into the new kernels per-deployment for staged rollout.

Compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless runtime flag or model profile selects the new kernels. Added fallbacks and validation tests to ensure numeric parity within float16 tolerances for our supported models.

Testing & rollout: unit tests for kernels and rope handling, integration perf runs on our perf-canary infra (A100, H100), e2e generation smoke tests with gpt-medium/gpt-large variants. Gradual rollout plan included in release notes to enable canary on 10% of serving traffic before wider rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Benchmarks against master for latency and p99 on A100/H100
- [x] Numeric parity tests added
- [x] CI passes (lint/build/unit)
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout config

Related: builds on work from pr-34211 and pr-41234 (previous FlashAttention upgrades) and closes ENG-1912 for improved rotary handling and ENG-2047 for fused-kernel scheduling improvements.
